jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer
jobs.description:
A global financial institution is seeking a hands-on Chief Information Security Officer to lead the Information Security program for its New York operation.

The role combines executive cybersecurity leadership with direct involvement in cyber risk, regulatory compliance, vulnerability management, remediation, incident readiness, and security governance. The successful candidate will inherit an established program and will be expected to evaluate the current environment, identify opportunities for continued improvement, and strengthen the organization's overall cybersecurity posture.

The CISO will work closely with senior business, risk, and technology leadership as well as a global Head Office security organization. Core architecture and engineering are largely managed globally, while the New York team maintains responsibility for local security oversight, regulatory obligations, risk management, remediation, and security-program leadership.

Responsibilities

Lead and continuously enhance the Information Security program.
Conduct cybersecurity risk assessments and identify opportunities to strengthen controls and governance.
Oversee cybersecurity regulatory compliance and annual certification activities.
Lead vulnerability-management and remediation oversight.
Maintain, test, and improve incident-response capabilities.
Review cybersecurity risk associated with new applications, vendors, systems, integrations, and business initiatives.
Partner with global security teams on architecture, engineering, shared infrastructure, and local regulatory requirements.
Lead a small cybersecurity team while remaining personally involved in important security issues.
Prepare cybersecurity reporting and communicate material risks to senior management.
Partner with Risk, Audit, Compliance, technology, and business stakeholders.

Role Requirements

15+ years of progressive Information Security or cybersecurity experience.
Experience owning or materially leading an enterprise Information Security program.
Strong cybersecurity risk, governance, vulnerability-management, and remediation experience.
Hands-on understanding of enterprise security controls and infrastructure.
Experience operating within a regulated environment.
Strong incident-response and cybersecurity-risk-assessment experience.
Executive-level written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work effectively with regulators, auditors, executives, risk organizations, and technical teams.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent in a relevant technical or security discipline.
Ability to work onsite in New York City four days per week.

Nice to Have

Banking or foreign banking organization experience.
CISSP, CISM, CCISO, CISA, or equivalent certification.
Master's degree.
Experience operating within a global security organization.
AI-security governance exposure.

jobs.title: IT Business Relationship Director, Americas
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Job Overview

We are hiring an IT Business Relationship Director to ensure IT service delivery meets the operational needs of program offices across the Americas geography (US and LATAM), translating business needs into IT priorities and IT technical capability into business value. The role sits at the intersection of IT and program operations — building trust with leadership, diagnosing where IT processes break down, and brokering the cross-office knowledge and escalation paths that don't currently exist structurally.

This role will operate as the connective layer between IT and Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) and Crisis, Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) leadership across the US and LATAM, working alongside the Global IT Solutions team, the Americas IT Service Desk (POD) and RAI Operations staff. They will build a regular engagement cadence with RAI office and CRRD program leadership, develop enough programmatic fluency to judge whether an IT solution will work in the field, own escalations, knowing when an issue needs IT leadership, a vendor, or executive attention. The role embeds proactive communication and cross-office knowledge-sharing into how IT and program operations work together, so that consistency across offices is structural rather than dependent on individual relationships.

The ideal candidate has direct experience in complex, distributed program operations, and brings credibility with program leadership as a result — not just IT service management experience. They are equal parts relationship manager, translator, and escalation owner: able to build trust with operations staff, assess whether a proposed IT solution will hold up in the field, and judge when to resolve something directly versus route it structurally. They have a bias for proactive communication, a high bar for consistency across offices, and a clear instinct for equipping program and office staff with the tools, access, and know-how to handle their own work.

This role reports to the Senior Director, IT Business Relationship Management and partners closely with RAI and CRRD leadership through an agreed engagement model. The role will also work closely with the Global IT Solutions Team, including the Service Delivery Center of Excellence, Helpdesk team, Enterprise Applications and Infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities

Relationship Management and Engagement

Serve as the senior IT partner to RAI office and CRRD program leadership, providing strategic guidance and thought partnership on IT service delivery performance, planned initiatives, and emerging risks across the US and LATAM
Maintain a regular engagement cadence with RAI operations directors and senior CRRD leadership, ensuring IT priorities are aligned with program needs and that leadership has visibility of service delivery against commitments
Act as the accountable IT point of contact for escalations from office and program leadership — owning the response, not just the routing
Build sufficient familiarity with the programmatic context of each cluster to advise credibly on whether IT solutions will work in practice, and to represent office needs accurately to HQ IT
Own cross-office knowledge brokering — surfacing what's working in one office to others, and serving as the connective point for "what are other offices doing on this?" questions that currently have no structural answer
Act as the strategic focal point for IT initiative rollouts across RAI offices and CRRD programs in the Americas – shaping appropriate timing, delivery and relaying infrastructure, application, and programmatic IT needs from offices to HQ IT teams and vice versa.
Support IT budget planning for the Americas region and ensure asset documentation, audit readiness, and regulatory compliance obligations are maintained

Escalation, Risk Management and Service Performance

Own escalation pathways for issues that fall between the helpdesk and engineering teams, knowing when to involve specific IT leads, vendors, or procurement and following through to resolution
Monitor service delivery performance and key performance indicators across the Americas region, identifying patterns and recurring issues that should trigger problem management review; escalate trending patterns as they emerge for either immediate action, system enhancement, or larger risk management
Partner with the Global Service Desk Manager on T1/T2 technician performance, ensuring ticket priority logic and SLA adherence

Job Requirements

Knowledge & Experience

6-8 years in a relationship management, business partnering, or program/operations role bridging technical and non-technical stakeholders — direct experience with humanitarian, nonprofit, or similarly complex distributed-operations environments strongly preferred
Working knowledge of the IT service and technology lifecycle, from planning and delivery through operations and continuous improvement, sufficient to engage credibly with technical teams and evaluate whether a proposed solution is fit for purpose
Familiarity with IT best-practice frameworks and delivery models (e.g., ITIL, Agile/Scrum, or equivalent project delivery methodologies) and how they apply to service management and technology rollouts; ITIL Foundation certification preferred, not required
Demonstrated experience translating operational needs into technical priorities and representing technical capability back to non-technical leadership
Experience defining and tracking performance metrics (KPIs, SLAs, or equivalent) and running a recurring review cadence with stakeholders

Personal Attributes

Spanish language proficiency
Builds credibility quickly with leadership
Comfortable holding ambiguity and structuring it
Strong written and verbal communication; able to translate fluently between technical and program audiences

Working Environment

This position is based in the US – Hybrid. The role may require travel to US and LATAM Offices as necessary.

Compensation:
(Pay Rate: $132,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

Professional Standards:
All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

Cookies: https://careers.rescue.org/us/en/cookiesettings

Benefits:
IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

Equal Opportunity Employer:
IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: VP, Global Technology Services
jobs.description:
About SH/FT

Shift Paradigm is an execution-led strategic consultancy that bridges the gap between enterprise strategy and technical reality. We partner with Fortune 500 brands and emerging leaders to solve the inherent complexity of modern digital marketing. As partners to the world’s leading MarTech platforms, including Adobe, Salesforce, Optimizely, and Braze, we deploy integrated experts across data analytics, marketing strategy, technology development, engineering, and revenue operations to ensure our clients’ tech stacks don't just exist, but perform.

The Role

SH/FT is seeking a VP of Global Technology Services to lead and scale our technology delivery practice across the Adobe and Salesforce ecosystems and web engineering. This is a senior leadership role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, develops processes with clarity, works cross-functionally by default, and is energized by building client relationships. You will own the quality, margin, and strategic direction of our technology services engagements from pre-sale through delivery, while unifying a cross-functional team of architects, engineers, and platform experts into a single, scalable practice.

This is not a role for someone who needs a fully defined playbook. It requires a leader who can move between executive strategy and hands-on execution when it counts, drive cross-functional alignment without formal authority, and bring clarity and momentum to complex, evolving client engagements spanning martech platform configuration to web and email engineering. You'll have real latitude to shape how this practice is structured, staffed, and grown.

What You’ll Lead

Client Delivery and Technical Strategy

Own technology services delivery across active engagements, ensuring technical quality, on-time delivery, and alignment to scope
Serve as a senior technical and strategic advisor to clients, translating complex architecture, engineering, and platform capabilities into clear business outcomes
Step in directly on client work where needed to protect delivery integrity - particularly on the most complex or highest-stakes engagements
Provide thought leadership in RFP and RFI responses, ensuring technical feasibility, clarity, and alignment with best practices
Establish and enforce architectural standards, delivery governance, and quality frameworks across the practice

Practice and Team Leadership

Lead, develop, and retain a team of Directors, senior architects, and engineers across the Adobe and Salesforce ecosystems and web engineering
Foster a culture of technical excellence, accountability, and continuous learning
Set standards and best practices for system integrations and email engineering, including responsive design, rendering compatibility, templating architecture, and deployment workflows
Identify opportunities for practice innovation, including accelerators, reusable frameworks, and AI and ML enablement
Partner with Sales and leadership on pipeline development, partnership co-selling, and capability positioning

Cross-Functional Process and Growth

Drive process and operating rhythm across a matrixed, cross-functional team where formal structure is still being built
Partner closely with Sales, Alliances, Business Operations, and Delivery Management to ensure seamless handoffs from pre-sale through execution
Build scalable delivery frameworks, scoping standards, and technical governance models that reduce variability and protect margin across platform and email work
Identify and close operational gaps before they become client or financial issues

What You Bring

Leadership and Delivery

10 or more years in marketing technology, solution architecture, software engineering, or digital consulting, with at least 3–5 years in a leadership role (Director or equivalent)
Proven track record leading delivery across multiple complex engagements simultaneously in a consulting or agency environment
Highly comfortable operating in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where process must be built alongside execution
Strong cross-functional influencer who drives alignment without relying on formal authority
Exceptional executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to lead client conversations at the VP and C-Suite level

Technical Expertise

Deep, hands-on expertise in at least one of the Adobe ecosystem (AEP, AEM, CDP, Marketo, AJO, CJA) or the Salesforce ecosystem (Marketing Cloud, Data Cloud, Account Engage, Agentforce, Sales Cloud), with working fluency across the other-
Strong background in email development, including HTML/CSS email engineering, responsive design, rendering across clients and devices, ESP integrations, and templating frameworks
Broad understanding of enterprise data architecture, identity resolution, and customer 360 strategy
Experience integrating martech platforms with data warehouses, CRMs, CMS platforms, and cloud infrastructure
Experience with AI and ML enablement across marketing and data platforms

About SH/FT

SH/FT is a client services business that focuses on implementing and activating technology and data to make sales and marketing work. Our people bring combined experience across technology, data and analytics, business strategy, and campaign operations to accelerate our clients' businesses. We keep pace with change in modern marketing and technology in order to create effective, scalable, and future-proof solutions for clients that span both the Fortune 500 and emerging industry leaders. We have built strong relationships with the world's most influential martech platforms and are key partners to them and their clients.

Why SH/FT

SH/FT is a consultancy built for transformation. We bridge the gap between marketing, data, and technology to unlock growth for some of the world's most recognized brands. As VP of Technology Services, you will shape how our clients connect with their customers through intelligent architecture, scalable delivery, and data-driven strategy - and you'll have significant influence over how the practice's structure, standards, and team are shaped and scaled. You will lead a team doing some of the most complex and interesting work in martech today, with a direct line to executive leadership and real influence over where the practice goes next.

This is a fully remote position. Candidates must be located in North America.

new_jobs.title: IT Business Relationship Director, Americas
new_jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Job Overview

We are hiring an IT Business Relationship Director to ensure IT service delivery meets the operational needs of program offices across the Americas geography (US and LATAM), translating business needs into IT priorities and IT technical capability into business value. The role sits at the intersection of IT and program operations — building trust with leadership, diagnosing where IT processes break down, and brokering the cross-office knowledge and escalation paths that don't currently exist structurally.

This role will operate as the connective layer between IT and Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) and Crisis, Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) leadership across the US and LATAM, working alongside the Global IT Solutions team, the Americas IT Service Desk (POD) and RAI Operations staff. They will build a regular engagement cadence with RAI office and CRRD program leadership, develop enough programmatic fluency to judge whether an IT solution will work in the field, own escalations, knowing when an issue needs IT leadership, a vendor, or executive attention. The role embeds proactive communication and cross-office knowledge-sharing into how IT and program operations work together, so that consistency across offices is structural rather than dependent on individual relationships.

The ideal candidate has direct experience in complex, distributed program operations, and brings credibility with program leadership as a result — not just IT service management experience. They are equal parts relationship manager, translator, and escalation owner: able to build trust with operations staff, assess whether a proposed IT solution will hold up in the field, and judge when to resolve something directly versus route it structurally. They have a bias for proactive communication, a high bar for consistency across offices, and a clear instinct for equipping program and office staff with the tools, access, and know-how to handle their own work.

This role reports to the Senior Director, IT Business Relationship Management and partners closely with RAI and CRRD leadership through an agreed engagement model. The role will also work closely with the Global IT Solutions Team, including the Service Delivery Center of Excellence, Helpdesk team, Enterprise Applications and Infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities

Relationship Management and Engagement

Serve as the senior IT partner to RAI office and CRRD program leadership, providing strategic guidance and thought partnership on IT service delivery performance, planned initiatives, and emerging risks across the US and LATAM
Maintain a regular engagement cadence with RAI operations directors and senior CRRD leadership, ensuring IT priorities are aligned with program needs and that leadership has visibility of service delivery against commitments
Act as the accountable IT point of contact for escalations from office and program leadership — owning the response, not just the routing
Build sufficient familiarity with the programmatic context of each cluster to advise credibly on whether IT solutions will work in practice, and to represent office needs accurately to HQ IT
Own cross-office knowledge brokering — surfacing what's working in one office to others, and serving as the connective point for "what are other offices doing on this?" questions that currently have no structural answer
Act as the strategic focal point for IT initiative rollouts across RAI offices and CRRD programs in the Americas – shaping appropriate timing, delivery and relaying infrastructure, application, and programmatic IT needs from offices to HQ IT teams and vice versa.
Support IT budget planning for the Americas region and ensure asset documentation, audit readiness, and regulatory compliance obligations are maintained

Escalation, Risk Management and Service Performance

Own escalation pathways for issues that fall between the helpdesk and engineering teams, knowing when to involve specific IT leads, vendors, or procurement and following through to resolution
Monitor service delivery performance and key performance indicators across the Americas region, identifying patterns and recurring issues that should trigger problem management review; escalate trending patterns as they emerge for either immediate action, system enhancement, or larger risk management
Partner with the Global Service Desk Manager on T1/T2 technician performance, ensuring ticket priority logic and SLA adherence

Job Requirements

Knowledge & Experience

6-8 years in a relationship management, business partnering, or program/operations role bridging technical and non-technical stakeholders — direct experience with humanitarian, nonprofit, or similarly complex distributed-operations environments strongly preferred
Working knowledge of the IT service and technology lifecycle, from planning and delivery through operations and continuous improvement, sufficient to engage credibly with technical teams and evaluate whether a proposed solution is fit for purpose
Familiarity with IT best-practice frameworks and delivery models (e.g., ITIL, Agile/Scrum, or equivalent project delivery methodologies) and how they apply to service management and technology rollouts; ITIL Foundation certification preferred, not required
Demonstrated experience translating operational needs into technical priorities and representing technical capability back to non-technical leadership
Experience defining and tracking performance metrics (KPIs, SLAs, or equivalent) and running a recurring review cadence with stakeholders

Personal Attributes

Spanish language proficiency
Builds credibility quickly with leadership
Comfortable holding ambiguity and structuring it
Strong written and verbal communication; able to translate fluently between technical and program audiences

Working Environment

This position is based in the US – Hybrid. The role may require travel to US and LATAM Offices as necessary.

Compensation:
(Pay Rate: $132,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

Professional Standards:
All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

Cookies: https://careers.rescue.org/us/en/cookiesettings

Benefits:
IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

Equal Opportunity Employer:
IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
